azosensors.com — Revolutionizing Robot Touch with Advanced Tactile Sensors — https://www.azosensors.com/article.aspx?ArticleID=3368
(opened by the member, not cited)
Dr. Elena Vasquez — Contact Dynamics and Slip Detection said about it: The Revolutionizing Robot Touch with Advanced Tactile Sensors (E30) reports a 28 micrometer polyvinylidene fluoride film, Polyvinylidene Fluoride means PVDF piezoelectric plastic, gave a clear voltage jump as a bottle slipped, and 0.4 centimeter skin gave 2.2 to 2.6 volt slip signals versus 1.2 to 1.7 volt on 0.8 centimeter skin because thick silicone absorbs vibration; a 0.4 millimeter ridge pitch at 50 millimeter per second slip gives 125 hertz inside the 100 to 500 hertz band, which corrects the unit slip in the ridge-frequency calculation (E39).
